reviews.review_text:
I find it hard to understand how this has such high ratings. To me - as a regular fine diner -
it’s a highly overrated restaurant. For 500 dollar for two for the tasting menu at least one should also get great service (besides great food). Instead the waiters just put plates in front of you, mumble a quick description and leave. There is no effort to establish rapport with the guests or an effort to make the guests feel great. Very disappointing. The food was good but felt too robotic - a series of neat plates, some quite tasteful but delivered with little charm. We were done with the menu within 2 hours. Again at this price level one can expect much more in terms of experience. Furthermore they seem to have a sewage problem as it smelled like that - especially downstairs. And it was uncomfortably cold in the upstairs dining room due to the air-con both which is why I rated low on atmosphere. The place does look nice though and there are lovely details in cutlery and plating.

Overall not worth booking 3 months ahead and spending this kind of money on. Go elsewhere.
A SUPER EXPERIENCE IN EVERY WAY,
The most delicious food I've ever eaten, everything was exquisite.

Book 3+ months ahead. Come here for intimate dinner focused on unique blend of ingredients, farm to table, simple and exceptional at the same time. We chose a 12-course tasting and paired it with non-alcoholic drinks. It was phenomenal. This really is a place where chefs come to eat. We spent 1450 soles for 2.

Tasting menu Spotify wrapped would include: 1.Scallops, sanky and jalapeno
2. Mamey, olluco and macambo
3. Cornbread
Amazing!
Creative and intriguing dishes that were finely executed. I usually dislike flan but the flan was heavenly. One of the best desserts I’ve had in my life.
Cozy place.

Fantastic experience! The Popeyes crab was a flavor bomb!!

Went for A La carte lunch but would for sure come back for the tasting menu if visiting Lima again!

An unmissable experience! We opted for the tasting menu, a pairing with both alcoholic and non-alcoholic wines. The cuisine features local and seasonal ingredients in a variety of dishes, not just classic Peruvian fare. A perfect blend.
It was a pleasure to taste such ingredients, and the plating was flawless—not at all pretentious, but clean, neat, and innovative.
The service was excellent, with each dish explained very well.

It's no wonder it's ranked as one of the best restaurants in the world!
My boyfriend and I booked dinner, and what a pleasant surprise Mérito was!
The ambiance is dimly lit, with few tables, a very intimate atmosphere in a wonderful house!!
The service was excellent!
And the tasting menu, oh my, what a dinner!! It's incredible how the chef manages to use local and not always well-known ingredients and enhance them in the way he does. One of the things I liked most in Lima was how the chefs value Peruvian ingredients, whether from the coast, mountains, or jungle! Everything was surprising, and each dish was better than the last.

It's a mix of curiosity and discovery of what's in front of you and what you'll feel when you eat. An explosion of intense and striking flavors that make the experience truly unforgettable!

I won't describe the dishes much so as not to spoil the surprise, but if you have any doubts, don't!!! Just go! I guarantee it will be etched in your memory forever!!!

It's important to point out that I don't eat meat, and for the main course they prepared something special for me, checking with my boyfriend beforehand to make sure it was something I really wanted. And my dish was wonderful, very well thought out!

Congratulations to the whole team!! 👏👏👏

One of the best restaurants in the world and in Latin America. Service was fantastic. Super tasty menu.

Scallops - 5/5
Salmon Tartare - 5/5
Fish Curry - 5/5
Chocolate Dessert - 5/5

The service was great. The entire menu looks delicious. The scallops were so fresh and light. I loved the salmon tartare. Super super tasty. Fish curry was fantastic. The dessert was rich and full of flavor.

reviews.review_text: Incredible food and service. Unique combinations and artful way of bringing out subtle flavors in each dish.

This restaurant is truly a five star experience, one of the best meals we have ever eaten and certainly some of the best service we’ve ever had. For one, our flight from Cusco to Lima was extremely late and the restaurant kept in contact with me via WhatsApp and saved our table past our original reservation time which I thought was incredible considering the limited space and completely full restaurant upon arrival. For dinner it is tasting menu only, and I felt that I got to taste a diverse spectrum of exquisite flavors that was the perfect level of filling but not too much food. Special call outs for dishes for us were the Yacon, fish, kiwicha and the beef arracache and mango (all of it was incredible). This is one of the best meals I have ever had.
A unique experience you must know about
A feast for the eyes. A delight for the palate.

Hidden Gem in Barranco! We enjoyed a wonderful lunch at this little establishment that packs a huge gastronomic experience. Make sure that you make a reservation as there are only about 10 tables and a log waiting list. My meal consisted of octopus that was prepared and presented extremely well. For the Main course, the fish curry was exquisite. White flaky tender and melt in your mouth goodness. The flavors were delicious and everything complimented the flavors. For dessert the “Roca” which is a chocolate rock that contained enjoyable amounts of sweet and savory. Make a reservation and go!

reviews.review_text: Having revitalized an old space with warm woods and careful lighting, the owners have created a charming restaurant that celebrates ‘essence’. From the raw beams and walls that hold the space, the chef has worked hard to showcase the flavours and ingredients that are quintessentially Peruvian. Delicate dishes play with texture, colour and temperature in ways that delight the eyes and palate, simply laid out on earthy plates and smooth ‘stoneware’. Prepared to be amazed.

Definitely not worth the hype or the price.

I’d been to Merito before a few times, and a la carte option was really good and reasonably priced.

Now it’s only tasting menu, which makes it 4X more expensive.  But the food, despite being creative and relatively good, was not memorable at all.

It was a disappointment.  I’m really surprised by such high reviews.  Maybe most of them come from the a la carte era.

Definitely not worth the price. And definitely not at Peru’s top list.  I dont know what happened to this place.  What a pity.

We had a fantastic experience with impeccable service and novel, exciting flavors as part of the tasting menu. We were continually blown away as each dish was brought out (I included a few fun pictures of some of my favorites). So many delicious tastes and exciting textures. We definitely had a few favorites but the entire menu was a delight. We felt the price was well worth it and the servers were very attendant throughout the night.  The sommelier was also lovely and helped us select a bottle of sparkling wine from Argentina for the evening.

We did the tasting menu.   It was an amazing dining experience with a menu pack full of uniquely combined Peruvian jungle and andean ingredients.  Love that their entrance goes through the kitchen!  Very accommodating staff that explained every dish and ingredient thoroughly.  They recommended a delicious Argentinian sparkling wine that enhanced the evening.  The scallops dish with jalapeños sauce was probably my favorite but it was hard to choose.  Many of their dishes looked stunningly simple but tasted much different than what you were expecting, which created many entertaining surprises.  Overall the meal was complete and well thought out, and we left very full/satisfied.
Excellent! A unique, innovative, and delicious option. Highly recommended.

Delicate, perfection is the word you can say about food in Merito.

The food was amazing. I really had great time in this restaurant. If you visit Lima and looking for high quality of restaurant.

Here is the one for you

Spectacular, one of my favorite restaurants. From the service to the food, everything was excellent, very attentive... the flavor and presentation of the dishes were superb. We wanted to go back for more.

Very modern and innovative menu with ingredients all sourced from Peru. The service was top notch as you'd expect with a restaurant of this caliber. Most of the dishes were very well balanced between flavors and textures. Would recommend to anyone visiting Lima and looking for a fine dining experience.
Very bad experience
reviews.author_name: Edgar Fabián De la Cruz Timana

reviews.review_text: Very attentive
Excellent
Mmm worth it
Everything is nice, but I think its target audience is tourists. The food is good, but gourmet. A lovely atmosphere, like all the others in Barranco.
Excellent respecter, you have delicious food and friendly service
It's an excellent place to go, the flavors are incredible and the service impeccable, highly recommended.

We ordered 5+1 things between two people and felt that it was enough food. Okay: popeye crab, white fish with cocona / Good: Scallops with sanki and jalapeño, Fish curry / Amazing: Lamb and tuber (tender and so succulent), Flan (soooo creamy with a slight burnt caramel taste on the sauce, the lightly bitter taste compliments the taste and texture of the custard very well). We also got the Chirimoya cocktail - taste was good, but also quite basic. I gave it 4 stars because only 1/5 dishes were really, really good in our opinion.

Service from Cesmar was 💯, she was very attentive and thorough in her explanation of the dishes. We found the price affordable for this level of dining experience. For reference, our meal came to around 260 PEN per person. I recommend booking in advance, but if you didn't, it's worth walking in to check if they have any availability for that day/the next couple of days (this is what we did). Happy dining! 🥳

I was amazed by the extraordinary cuisine, beautifully presented dishes, and delicious food.
I followed the waiter's recommendations, all of which were spot-on.
There are some excellent gluten-free options.
Highly recommended.
Top notch restaurant in Lima, definitely recommended, pricey but i do not think you can try these dishes somewhere else.
Beautiful place for a date! Not cheap, be ready to pay😊 but this experience definitely worth it

The food was really really really good and I wonder if I am being way too generous with my 3/5 rating. My wife made it clear to one of the waiters she was allergic to mango when she saw it was on the menu (we mentioned shellfish and tree nuts in our reservation but told them about mango verbally). The waiter told her not to worry, it is only a side and not in the main portion of the course. Fair enough, but they still brought it out with her food. She asked them what had mango in it and when she told me she had an allergy again the waitress (different server then who she originally told) took it away. Luckily my wife asked, if she hadn't, it could have been a very dangerous situation. Everything else was spectacular other then that, but I can't forgive that major mistake.

One of the best dinners I can remember.  The flavors were out of this world. Several of the dishes I will dream about for quite a while.  The ambiance, the music, the staff. Five stars across the board! Really glad we read all the reviews and chose this as our last meal in Lima. Do not miss!
Tremendous! A unique experience. The combination of incredible flavors and sublime service. Highly recommended.
Wonderful ambiente and extraordinary food - huge portions at a very fair pricepoint, being the 23rd best restaurant in the world! 10/10 recommend!

We ate at Merito last night and it was one of the best dining experiences I've ever had.  The tasting menu was fantastic and the wine pairing was perfect.  There wasn't a single thing we did not like.  The atmosphere was great with the smell of classic cedarwood in the dining room.  We've eaten at several fine dining restaurants in Lima for the last few days, but Merito was our hands down favorite.  You won't be disappointed.

Go.

If you're reading reviews, you're probably wondering if the place is worth a visit. Chances are you've come to value this visit because of the 50 Best list and are undecided about whether to visit a place ranked 26th on the list, or the #1 spot that you're fortunate enough to be in today's city that also ranks #1 on the list.

I've had the opportunity to travel to Lima four times with my wife. I'm a sincere fan of its cuisine. Although I'm not dedicated to the industry, nor am I a cook or chef, the gastronomy of this city moves me to my core (this isn't the place to tell you all this and make this post longer).

On these trips, we've had the opportunity to visit several restaurants and cuisines from several renowned chefs, not only from this country but from around the world.

On my first visit, and being new to this whole thing, I went straight to the cornerstone of Peruvian cuisine and dedicated my entire trip to experiencing Gastón Acurio's cuisine, ranging from Papachos to Astrid y Gastón, while also crossing paths with La Mar and Tanta. Since that first trip in 2019, it seemed incredible to me how they've managed to capture so much attention for us tourists through cuisine.
On subsequent visits, we've had the opportunity to experience and taste Central by Virgilio Martínez, Maido by Mitsuharu "Micha" Tsumura (which was our top restaurant before this visit to Mérito; we went in 2022 if I'm not mistaken), Rafael by Rafael Osterling, among several others. I mention these because they're probably places you're considering visiting.

Now, getting to the real deal: the experience at Mérito by Juan Luis Martínez.
It was something different, something intimate, with precise service that didn't make you feel overwhelmed, pleasant, and they gave you the time you needed to savor each dish and each drink (we had a tasting menu with wine pairing). The space was small, with warm lighting and nothing glamorous, but that allowed you to fully concentrate on what matters: the food and the experience. There wasn't a single dish on the menu I wouldn't have liked to eat. This often happens at other tastings, mostly because your palate is often so unaccustomed to dishes or ingredients from the region that you honestly end up not liking one or two dishes on the menu. Here, everything was good for us, something as simple as the corn bread (pan de choclo, or corn bread) was beyond words, something so simple that it dazzles you in such a way (I even wanted to order another one to go). As we Mexicans would say, "the good vibes" of all the staff is something to be appreciated. You can tell at every moment that there's a good relationship between the entire team, and this is something that makes you feel comfortable. In the end, we had the opportunity to take a photo in the kitchen with practically the entire staff on duty at the time. I didn't notice it at the time, but looking back at my photo later, everyone was very welcoming and appeared in the photo practically as if they had plenty of free time to pose (I understand that this part is probably how they should do it due to protocol, but it's one thing to do it and another to do it well). As a curious fact, there was a person in the kitchen who served me last year at Central who gave me the tour and explanation of the Central restaurant. If I remember correctly, she's Chilean. Honestly, she seemed more relaxed, in a good way.

In conclusion, "GO!" Enjoy it and make the most of it. It has been our best gastronomic experience in Lima. It will definitely climb that list year after year. Take this review for what it is: a review, the honest opinion of a simple diner.

Ultimately, congratulations to the entire team that makes this possible.

If you only go to one of the big restaurants in Lima - make it this one!!! By far our favourite restaurant experience of all time. The food was incredible, bold and playful flavours with very interesting and creative presentation. Compared to the other restaurant we tried (I won't name names), Merito had far tastier food while still experimenting and being interesting.

We are vegan and the chef made an entirely vegan experience for us that did NOT compromise on creativity or flavour. The vegan versions went beyond making direct substitutions for non vegan ingredients; many of our dishes were entirely different than the standard menu for the evening. The chef even came to the table to talk to us about the meal and make sure that we were enjoying the vegan food.

Well worth the price tag. Do it!
Exciting ingredients in a creative cuisine. The ambient is correct with an interesting soundtrack.

Unforgettable dining experience to round up a visit to Peru

The concept of the menu overall, pairing of ingredients and textures are sophisticated and unique. Peru is known for its fantastic cuisine but Merito is just next level.

The staff is exceptionally attentive and knowledgeable. We got interesting explanations about the dishes we were trying and the origins of ingredients.

My biggest recommendation in Lima!

A tremendous culinary offering, with top-quality flavors and textures, paired with a consistent and high-quality pairing.

Special mention goes to two dishes: the conch shell and the Andean curry.

A 10/10 experience, a must-visit!

Definitely a must visit restaurant in Lima! Tasted ingredients and flavors that I have never tasted before! Love their wines as well, they have stuff like royal tokaji by the glass! The mains are very generous portions and desserts were phenomenal. I love that they focus on the quality of the food, and the restaurant itself (I mean the interior design and the signage) is extremely lowkey and humble. Service was really great as well!

8/2025 I've visted Mérito for the second (and third times). The first time, I ate the 12-course tasting menu for dinner. That receipt (for 2) is pictured. It is one of the more "affordable" tasting menus in Lima at PE 590 each. It was very good and well worth the relative price (relative to the other high-end restaurants). It is just not quite as "upscale" as some of the others. On my third visit (my daughter's second) was for the a la carte lunch. I realized that the menu was not very vegetarian friendly. I tried to order mostly vegetarian dishes for her and ended up primarily with deserts! The "air" cake was both of our favorites (the rectangular yellowish thing pictured once with the ovalish item on top and another time pictured beside on the same plate). Chef Martinez's deserts are the best. I unfortunately didn't try the Flan. My original suggestion of coming with a group of friends and ordering most of the lunch menu still holds. This restaurant is still a top 5 dining destination in Lima. Lastly, our server, Sergio (I hope I'm remembering his name correctly), was AMAZING. His English was flawless because his mother teaches English and he loves American movies.
8/2024 Mérito was tied for my #2 favorite restaurant in Lima. Unlike most of the other top restaurants, there is no chef’s tasting menu; it is a la carte. Therefore, I recommend inviting three friends and ordering the entire menu. Seriously. This place was so good and I wanted to try everything. Unfortunately, I only had the jalapeño scallops, the pork belly, and the chocolate rock (which starts with no hole). And my meal was less than $100 USD including tip which is downright affordable compared to the tasting menus at all the standard top restaurants (Central, Kjolle, Mayta, Maido, Astrid & Gaston which all cost PEN 1000 and up).
Couldn’t fault anything! Incredible experience and food from start to finish

Minimalist, avant-garde, but with all the flavor of the land. I would definitely return. Incredible design and staging. It was a pleasure to have enjoyed this fusion of talent and love for gastronomy.

The meal was exceptional and is one of the best I have ever had. Honestly tasting menus make me a little nervous because I wonder if the imagination of the chef is just too far outside my comfort zone. Despite my nerves, I brought an open mind to this experience.

As I reviewed the menu, cornbread jumped off the page. As a person who grew up eating cornbread, I was SURE that I would be disappointed. I have been to many restaurants who try to put some flare on cornbread and they fail. Well, it was not like Jiffy or any cornbread I have made from scratch. It was more like a sweet bread and the onion butter was wonderful. I was getting full but still regret I did not eat my last slice.

I could go on and rave about almost every dish but who wants to read all of that and I assume the menu changes so it is not even helpful. But I need to say the beef was fantastic. I do not eat much red meat and was set to be underwhelmed and it was amazing. And since my review seems to be all sunshine, I will be real and say there was one part I did not like and it was a gelatinous portion of a dessert. It is a texture I do not enjoy but it was such a small component of the meal that if you feel the same way this will not really impact your satisfaction. What can I say, it is just my palate.

By the dessert courses, I was pretty full any way but I managed to eat all of the thin cookies which gave me another surprise ….I enjoyed the white chocolate one. I generally love dark chocolate, will eat milk chocolate but pass on desserts with a white chocolate base. I was wrong again. This was great.

I wish I had photos of all the courses. They were a treat for the eyes not just the stomach.  I would go back in heartbeat. This was my best of many great meals in Lima.

An incredible experience. Each dish was an explosion of flavors. The cocktails were excellent, without excessive alcohol. The espresso to finish was delicious. They use specialty Cajamarca coffee from one of the best coffee shops in Lima, Milimétrica.

As for the service, they were very friendly and helpful. The atmosphere and decor were cozy. The dishes made in a local workshop went very well with each dish.
Excellent culinary experience, super delicious dishes and quality service
Highly recommended

A good restaurant that fuses flavors. It's small but cozy. I enjoyed the pancetta, and the appetizer was interesting, but honestly, what dazzled me the most was the flan. Delicious!! 10/10. I'd give everything else a 9/8. It's a place for a special occasion. I had lunch here with my girlfriend for our anniversary and enjoyed it. Recommended!
Their customer service is atrocious, they do not respect their clients.

I easily return to this place. It's extraordinary. As a foreigner, every bite was experience after experience of flavors I'd never tasted before, all of exceptional quality. It's not just food, it's an experience.
Long live El Capitan! The corn puree is top-notch, and I'm going to say the flan (just like at Clon) gets 5 stars! The menu isn't very extensive, but it has its special features.
A must try . For me, the best fine dining restaurant in Lima.

We went to Peru for my mom’s birthday this year. After spending a few days in Cusco, we came to Lima to actually have a proper birthday dinner. And our destination was Merito. The whole experience was magical. The setup, the lighting, the service and THE FOOD!  The pairing! Definitely one of the best dining experiences I had!!
A beautiful experience with wonderful personalized treatment that makes you feel pampered 😍🔥
One of the capital's must-visit restaurants. Go there with your eyes closed if your budget allows.

Oh gosh, what an outstanding meal! Tucked inside a narrow shophouse in Barranco, Mérito was the biggest surprise of our Lima trip, and easily our favorite restaurant.

Every single dish on the tasting menu was on point: bold, playful, and bursting with texture. Think smoky, grilled, fermented, pickled layered flavor.

Their natural wine selection was a revelation, offering a rare glimpse into South American winemaking.

Even more surreal: this was our very first meal in Peru, after 30+ hours of travel, it was still the same day we left. It’s a spot that froze in time for us. :)

Add to that the gorgeous interior, relaxed energy, and great service. Highly recommend!

This has been an ode to gastronomy, thank you Juan Luis and team for making this possible! It was one of my highlights of visiting Lima and you've outdone yourselves!

THANK YOU

Our experience at Mérito was simply fantastic! Without a doubt, it's among our favorite restaurants and was one of the best gastronomic experiences we've ever had. The atmosphere is super intimate, with charming decor and impeccable service; the waiters were extremely attentive and explained each dish in detail, ingredient by ingredient.

Our orders were:

For appetizers, we chose Scallops, sanki and jalapeño; the scallops were incredible, delicate, and visually resembled a work of art. We also ordered the Yacon, white fish and amaranthus, a dish so beautiful that we wanted to take it home. The base resembles potato, with a flavorful fish filling; besides being delicious, it's a true sensory experience!

For the main course, we tried the Glazed pork belly with arepas, a succulent pork belly accompanied by a delicious arepa—simply fantastic. We also ordered the fish curry; honestly, it was the most flavorful fish I've ever eaten!

To finish with a flourish, the dessert: Chocolate Rock, extraordinary! An explosion of flavor, texture, and presentation. Very, very good! There were two more desserts that we loved: the ice creams, the best in the world, and another one that was similar to a chocolate bar, which I confess I don't remember the name of, and it was okay.

Regarding the price: it's not cheap, but compared to the level of the experience and the restaurant, it's worth every penny. Anywhere else in the world, a meal of this level would cost much more!

I was thrilled to be able to eat lunch as a walk-in on a recent weekday. One of the best meals I’ve had in a long time, and definitely one of the highlights of my trip to Peru. Exemplary service (thank you, Sergio). Delicious, creative, inventive food at reasonable prices in a lovely, unpretentious setting.

Easy 5/5. Deserves all the accolades it’s received.

Delicious experience giving vibe of cool trendy of Lima, the staffs service were excellent, the wine pairing was exciting using regional wines , beautiful dishes. I took one star off bc of the mains of Amazonian fish and the curry were really not to my likings, I only had a bit of each tasting dishes.

The simplicity of a cup of tea.
The magic in the kitchen.
Architecture on a plate.
The exquisite setting. It blends your innocence, your past, and your present.
Looking at the walls took me back to my childhood; savoring each experience at my table brought me to the present.
An exquisite experience. ✍️
Perfection.
A meal here will change your life. Sit at the bar and watch them make art out of the freshest and most unique ingredients
Great experience!
Very enjoyable experience - great food and cocktails, and excellent service.
